solution: Four tosses give \(2^4 = 16\) equally likely outcomes. Exactly 3 heads can happen in \(\binom{4}{3} = 4\) ways, so the probability is \(\frac{4}{16} = \frac{1}{4}\).
Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4, which is 2 of the 6 faces. The probability is \(\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\).
A deck has 26 red cards (hearts and diamonds) out of 52. The probability is \(\frac{26}{52} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Of the 36 outcomes, 6 give a sum of 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2) and (6,1). The probability is \(\frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}\).
There are 10 balls and \(3 + 2 = 5\) of them are not red. The probability is \(\frac{5}{10} = \frac{1}{2}\).
The only way to get no head is TT, with probability \(\frac{1}{4}\). So at least one head has probability \(1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\).
There are 4 kings and 4 queens, 8 cards in all, and none is both. The probability is \(\frac{8}{52} = \frac{2}{13}\).
Two of the 10 tickets win, so the probability is \(\frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}\).
The first card is an ace with probability \(\frac{4}{52}\), and then the second with probability \(\frac{3}{51}\). Both are aces with probability \(\frac{4}{52} \times \frac{3}{51} = \frac{1}{221}\).
Four of the 8 sections (2, 4, 6, 8) are even. The probability is \(\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\).

note: TWIN: A=B (6/10 x 5/9 = 30/90 = 1/3 = 15/45); both are correct expressions
solution: Two white balls can be chosen in \(\binom{6}{2} = 15\) ways out of \(\binom{10}{2} = 45\) pairs. The probability is \(\frac{15}{45} = \frac{1}{3}\).
Only 3 and 6 are divisible by 3, which is 2 of the 6 faces. The probability is \(\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\).
Three coins give 8 outcomes, and exactly two tails occurs in 3 of them: TTH, THT and HTT. The probability is \(\frac{3}{8}\).
There are 13 hearts in 52 cards. The probability is \(\frac{13}{52} = \frac{1}{4}\).
The multiples of 5 from 1 to 20 are 5, 10, 15 and 20, four numbers. The probability is \(\frac{4}{20} = \frac{1}{5}\).
There are 6 doublets, (1,1) to (6,6), among the 36 outcomes. The probability is \(\frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}\).
The box holds \(8 + 5 + 7 = 20\) balls, 5 of them blue. The probability is \(\frac{5}{20} = \frac{1}{4}\).
Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together, so their probabilities add: \(P(A \cup B) = 0.4 + 0.5 = 0.9\).
A sum of 10 comes from (4,6), (5,5) and (6,4), 3 of the 36 outcomes. The probability is \(\frac{3}{36} = \frac{1}{12}\).
Five of the 15 people are women. The probability is \(\frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\).
A deck has 26 black cards (spades and clubs) out of 52. The probability is \(\frac{26}{52} = \frac{1}{2}\).

note: checked: 5 ways for 4 heads + 1 way for 5
solution: Five tosses give 32 outcomes. Exactly 4 heads happens in \(\binom{5}{4} = 5\) ways and 5 heads in 1 way, so at least 4 heads has probability \(\frac{6}{32} = \frac{3}{16}\).
Three of the 12 balls are red. The probability is \(\frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}\).
For independent events the probabilities multiply: \(P(A \cap B) = 0.6 \times 0.7 = 0.42\).
The perfect squares from 1 to 25 are 1, 4, 9, 16 and 25, five numbers. The probability is \(\frac{5}{25} = \frac{1}{5}\).
Neither green nor red means yellow: 5 of the \(4 + 5 + 6 = 15\) marbles. The probability is \(\frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\).
A product of 12 comes from (2,6), (6,2), (3,4) and (4,3), 4 of the 36 outcomes. The probability is \(\frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}\).

note: Stem garbled: 'all cards except aces removed' leaves only the aces; read as 'the four aces removed', which matches '48 cards'.
solution: Removing the 4 aces takes out the ace of hearts too, leaving 12 hearts among 48 cards. The probability is \(\frac{12}{48} = \frac{1}{4}\).
An event either happens or does not, so the two probabilities add to 1. The probability that it happens is \(1 - 0.25 = 0.75\).
The set has 9 numbers, and 2, 3, 5 and 7 are prime. The probability is \(\frac{4}{9}\).
